title: Bar Hamadura
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was Shmuel’s student: in Yoma 87a, Bar Hamadura says, “I was standing before Shmuel.” In [Shabbat 125a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.125a.2) and [Menachot 38b](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.38b.10), Bar Hamadura speaks in Shmuel’s name; [Shabbat 107b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.107b.12) has Mar bar Hameduri speaking in Shmuel’s name (Hyman reports that Dikdukei Soferim omits Mar). Hyman infers that he lived a long life, citing [Shabbat 107b:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.107b.12), [125a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.125a.2), and [Yevamot 83b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.83b.10), where Rava says, “Bar Hameduri explained it to me.” Rav Avdimi bar Hameduri is also found in [Sukkah 20a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.20a.10).[^3][^4]

notes.text: In the checked Shabbat passage, Rava says that Bar Hameduri explained the matter to him. “Rava Bar Hameduri” in the earlier English incorrectly fused the speaker and the cited teacher.

The long-life conclusion is Hyman’s inference. The consulted Shabbat 107b distinguishes Rava, who speaks, from Bar Hameduri, who explained the matter to him. The exact Dikdukei Soferim omission was not independently inspected.

The consulted Shabbat and Menachot have Bar Hameduri transmit in Shmuel’s name, and Shabbat 107b calls him Mar. In Yevamot, Rava says that Bar Hameduri explained a teaching to him. Hyman uses the latter transmission to infer longevity. The selected Shabbat 107b passage is the transmission from Shmuel. The episode of Rava being told the explanation is directly linked at Yevamot.

At Shabbat 107b, Mar bar Hameduri first reports Shmuel’s ruling, then Rava says that Bar Hameduri explained it to him. At Shabbat 125a, Bar Hameduri likewise reports Shmuel, and Rava credits him with the explanation. Hyman infers longevity from the two attributions.
